LESSON: CAPACITY

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurement 2.1 Length 10
Topic 2.4: Capacity

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Capacity. Read, look at the pictures, practise, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: LEARN

Today, we are going to learn about how to use a half litre container and a quarter litre container to measure capacity. In this lesson, we will require the following. Five one litre plastic bottles. Two half litre plastic bottles. Water. A marker, a cutting tool, variety of containers, a notebook and a pencil or a pen. Welcome to Mathematical for Grade four. Today, we shall learn on how to use half quarter container and a quarter litre container to measure capacity. In grade three, we learned about measuring capacity in litres. This is an example to remind us how to measure capacity in litres. This is an example to remind us how to measure capacity in litres. Twenty five one litre bottles fills a bucket. What is the capacity of the bucket? I will repeat. Twenty five one litre bottle fills a bucket. What is the capacity of the bucket? If you say 25 litres, then you are correct. If you say 25 litres, then you are correct. Learner. Get two one litre plastic bottle. Get two one litre plastic bottle. Fill one bottle with water, that is the one litre plastic bottle. Fill one bottle with water, that is the one litre plastic bottle. Pour Water from the full one litre plastic bottle into the empty one litre plastic bottle until the levels in the two one litre plastic bottles are the same. Pour Water from the full one litre plastic bottle into the empty one litre plastic bottle until the levels in the two one litre plastic bottles are the same. Cut to one of the one litre plastic bottle with water at the level of water to make a half litre bottle. I will repeat. Cut one of the one litre plastic bottle with water at the level of water to make a half litre bottle. Learner How many half litres do we have in one litre? How many half litres do we have in one litre? You are correct, if you said two. very good.

Learner, get another one litre plastic bottle apart from the one we have used above and two half litre plastic bottles. Get another one little plastic bottle apart from the one we have used above and two half litre plastic bottles. Fill one of the half litre plastic bottle with water. Fill one of the half litre plastic bottle with water. Pour the water into the half litre plastic bottle which is empty, until the levels in the two half little plastic bottles are the same. Pour the water from the first filled half litre plastic bottle into the empty half litre plastic bottle until the levels in the two half litre plastic bottles are the same. Now cut one of the half litre plastic bottles at the level of water to make a quarter litre bottle. Cut one of the half litre plastic bottles at the level of the water to make a quarter litre bottle. Very good learner. We now have a half litre container and a quarter litre container. We have a half litre container and a quarter litre container. The following activity will help you understand more about measuring capacity using a half litre container or a quarter litre container. The following activity will help you understand more about measuring capacity using a half litre container and a quarter litre container. How many half litres are in each of the following? How many half litres are in each of the following? A. One litre. One litre. B. Ten litres. Ten litres. C. five litres. Five Litres. D. Two litres. Two Litres. Learner. How many quarter litres are in each of the following? A one litre. One litre. B. Two Litres. Two Litres. C. three litres. Three litres. D. six litres. six Litres. With that, we come to the end of our lesson today. Share your answers with your parents, guardian or friends. Until you meet again. Goodbye. Your radio teacher was Scholah Mkando. The program was written and produced by the It was recorded by John Mbithi for the Institute of Curriculum Development. Until next time, Goodbye.

SECTION 3: TRY THIS

1. Look again at the examples or pictures above.
2. Tell a parent or friend what Capacity means, using your own words.
3. Copy one example into your exercise book and change it to fit your school or home.
4. Underline three new words and find out what they mean.

SECTION 4: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Capacity.
2. Complete any “Work to do” items shown in the pupil book pages above.
3. Create three of your own practice questions on this topic.
4. Answer the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after finishing.

SECTION 5: REMEMBER

1. Topic: Capacity
2. Subject: MATHEMATICS
3. Learning materials: Maths Pro 5 measure capacity; Maths Prg 6 addition of capacity ; Maths Pro 7 subtract capacity 
4. Revise with the quiz now.
